question: The International Court of Justice has issued a historic advisory opinion in which it concludes that every State is obliged to protect the global climate system under international law.

This obligation includes due avoidance of significant damage to the environment (paragraphs 132 to 139), a requirement for States to cooperate with each other in good faith on the issue (paragraphs 140 to 142) and a requirement to guarantee environmental protection for present and future generations through applying the principle of intergenerational equity (paragraphs 155 to 157).

In addition, the Court states that failure to comply with these obligations constitutes an internationally wrongful act that has legal consequences (paragraph 409), such as ceasing unlawful acts or omissions, ensuring that they will not be repeated and paying full reparations for damages caused (paragraphs 446 to 455). Considering the above: 1.
What is the Commission’s view on the International Court of Justice’s advisory opinion?
Will the Commission promote any specific initiatives to boost compliance with these international obligations within the European Union?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.9.2025) The Commission welcomes the Advisory Opinion of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on climate change, which broadly reflects the EU’s position as submitted to the ICJ proceedings. The Court confirms the importance of the challenge faced and the importance of climate and environmental protection efforts.

It also reaffirms the obligation for States to cooperate and take collective and ambitious climate and environmental measures. The Commission does not envisage specific action as an immediate follow-up to the Advisory Opinion.

The Commission considers that its proposal for a 2040 target of a reduction of net greenhouse gas emissions of 90% compared to 1990 levels, including starting from 2036 a possible limited contribution of high-quality credits from outside the EU, is in line with its obligations under the Paris Agreement and international law, and calls on co-legislators for a swift political agreement on the 2040 target so as to enable the communication of an Nationally Determined Contribution ahead of the next COP30 in Belem.

The Commission will continue to lead international efforts to stay on the Paris Agreement trajectory, and to further develop, implement and enforce EU climate and environmental policies to comply with the obligations and commitments under other applicable law specifically identified by the ICJ.
